title: jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile
why_read: A reverse-engineered compatibility layer bringing a major PC/console game natively to iOS and macOS is a technically impressive feat of systems and emulation work, though legally murky.
analysis: This project claims to let people run their own licensed copy of Diablo II: Resurrected natively on iPhone, iPad, and Mac, implying significant work reimplementing or wrapping platform APIs, graphics, and input handling. Built in C with over 3,700 stars, it likely required deep reverse engineering of game internals and non-trivial porting work across radically different hardware and OS constraints. This kind of project is technically interesting to systems programmers interested in emulation, API shims, and cross-platform porting. The main caveat is the project's legal standing is uncertain since it touches a commercial game's internals, though it claims users must supply their own game files.
